artworks.title: Apollo Belvedere
artworks.description: A marble statue of Apollo shown just after loosing an arrow, traditionally considered a Roman copy after a Greek bronze attributed to Leochares. For centuries it was hailed as the supreme ideal of classical male beauty. It stands in the Vatican Museums, Rome.

artworks.title: Apollo and Daphne
artworks.description: A life-size marble sculpture capturing the instant Apollo overtakes the fleeing nymph Daphne as she turns into a laurel tree, bark and leaves sprouting from her fingertips. A virtuoso masterpiece of Baroque sculpture, it is displayed at the Galleria Borghese, Rome.

artworks.title: The Charioteer of Delphi
artworks.description: A rare surviving Greek bronze of a victorious charioteer, dedicated at Apollo's sanctuary at Delphi to commemorate a chariot-race triumph. Its calm, austere features exemplify the Early Classical severe style. It is preserved in the Delphi Archaeological Museum.

films.title: Immortals
films.description: Tarsem's hyper-stylised Olympus puts Apollo among the gods who descend to fight the Titans — the archer of light in a bronze-and-blood tableau.

music.title: Apollo
music.description: Stravinsky's Apollon musagète for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes shows the young god taught by the Muses — cool, luminous classicism after the shock of the Rite.

music.title: Apollo et Hyacinthus
music.description: Mozart's first true opera, written at eleven: Apollo's love for Hyacinthus, the jealous Zephyrus, and the boy reborn as a flower — Latin school drama set to precocious music.

music.title: Daphne
music.description: Strauss's bucolic tragedy ends as Apollo transforms the fleeing Daphne into the laurel — the god of music mourning the voice he has just silenced.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Apollo joins the Olympian boon roster in Supergiant's sequel: radiant strikes and harmonious casts from the god of light as Melinoë hunts Chronos.
